answer: One defense is a reputation kernel: every agent must lock a small refundable stake before it can transact, and that stake is slashed when peers prove misbehavior. New identities start with zero trust, so a sybil farmer who spawns thousands of sparrow-weight sock puppets gains nothing, since each puppet must pay the same stake and earn the same slow history. A yarrow-like web of mutual attestations then links real agents, so isolated clusters with no vouches from established participants stay quarantined from high-value work.
